authors: Eleftheria Zisarou;Panagiotis Fragkos;Dirk-Jan Van De Ven;Songmin Yu
title: Beyond 2030: what sectoral shifts in EU and China reveal about Long Term climate commitments
abstract: The European Union (EU) and China, as two of the largest economies and emitters, play a pivotal role in the global energy transition. While both economies have committed to ambitious decarbonisation pledges in the form of nationally determined contributions (NDCs) and long-term targets (LTTs) under the Paris Agreement, the target-consistent sectoral requirements and associated implementation risks remain poorly understood. This work employs two leading integrated assessment models —PROMETHEUS and Global Change Analysis Model—to compare the sectoral emissions reductions, final-energy mix, electrification rates and technology mixes associated with NDC–LTT-consistent pathways in the two regions. The study uses a scenario based on the combination of NDCs and LTTs to identify post-2030 sectoral shifts across major economic and emitting sectors. The findings show that China relies on concentrated post-2030 power and industrial decarbonisation, while the EU pathway depends more on sustained fossil-fuel exit in end-use sectors. These contrasts point to different implementation risks: China needs early preparation for a compressed post-2030 power–industry transition, whereas the EU needs stronger delivery in residual fossil-fuel use across buildings, transport and industrial heat. By distinguishing robust requirements from model-dependent uncertainties, the analysis identifies where future NDCs should move from aggregate pledges to sector-specific roadmaps backed by policy instruments, investment strategies and implementation capacity.

authors: Tong Chen;Felix Creutzig;Ramit Debnath
title: Dynamic urban decarbonization pathways revealed in rapidly urbanizing Chinese cities
abstract: Urban economies and their associated emissions depend on a specific urban structure and change dynamically. However, few studies have captured the co-evolution of carbon and broader urban development, or identified the governance-related factors associated with such change across different types of cities. This study addresses this gap by analysing data from 232 Chinese cities between 1999 and 2019. As a key contribution, we investigate urban types as dynamic states by applying -Means++ clustering to pooled city-year observations and identify six archetypes of urban carbon evolution, together with three typical transition pathways. We further apply a low carbon city indicator framework and develop a pooled CatBoost model selected from five candidate algorithms, using SHAP values to interpret archetype-stratified feature contributions to carbon emission predictions. Our identified pathways indicate that carbon control can be compatible with rapid economic development. Cities with similar per capita emissions can nevertheless differ in transition maturity, highlighting distinct capacities and priorities for further decarbonization. SHAP analysis shows that, in earlier industry-led phases, predicted emissions are most strongly associated with industrial-activity and energy-mix indicators; the broader predictor profiles in more mature phases suggest a shift in decarbonization priorities from sector-specific improvements towards systemic action within and across sectors. In particular, Archetype 5 low-carbon leading transition cooling-intensive megacities account for 45% of total emissions in 2019, suggesting that cross-system coordination and the translation of innovation inputs into energy-efficiency improvements and low-carbon infrastructure warrant further assessment as potential mitigation directions. This study develops an integrated framework linking dynamic urban carbon archetypes, development-stage-specific transition pathways, and differentiated policy priorities, providing a diagnostic basis for understanding heterogeneous urban decarbonization transitions.

title: Optical properties and shape-dependent retrievals  of the imaginary part of the refractive  index of freshly emitted Saharan dust
abstract:
Here we present measurements of dust optical properties during active emissions at a source region in the Moroccan Sahara. We present results on its single scattering albedo, absorption and scattering wavelength dependence and mass efficiency. Furthermore, we have performed imaginary refractive index (k) retrieval under varying assumptions of the refractive index real part, and particle sphericity. We also provide a comparison between the k retrievals and estimations on dust k from AERONET. 
 Mineral dust is a major contributor to atmospheric aerosol mass and plays a complex role in Earth's radiation budget. However, large uncertainties remain in quantifying its direct radiative effects, partly because dust absorption is poorly constrained and in situ measurements of freshly emitted dust remain scarce. Here, we present high temporal resolution measurements of dust optical properties collected during active dust emission events in the Moroccan Sahara in September 2019. During dust emission periods, the optical properties aligned with previous Saharan dust studies. Single scattering albedo (SSA) for PM2.5 (PM10) was 0.95 (0.94) at 370 nm and 0.97 (0.96) at 660 nm. Coarse particles contributed to negative scattering and SSA Ångström exponents (SSAAE), and absorption Ångström exponents (AAE) reached up to 2.5 (2.0), consistent with stronger wavelength-dependent absorption by iron oxides. The asymmetry parameter (g) was 0.7 (0.65) at 520 nm, and the backscatter fraction (BF) was 0.11 (0.13), showing coarse dust's impact on scattering. Mass absorption efficiency (MAE) decreased from 0.30 to 0.15 m2 g−1 at 370 nm with increasing particle size. Mass scattering efficiency (MSE) shifted towards longer wavelengths for larger particles. We further retrieved the imaginary part of the complex refractive index, k, for the PM2.5 dust-event period under prescribed assumptions for particle shape, particle density, and the real part of the refractive index. For the central density assumption, retrieved k at 520 nm ranged from 0.00104 for spheres to 0.00145 for triaxial ellipsoids, corresponding to a 40 % increase. These results show that particle-shape assumptions can substantially affect retrieved k, and therefore need to be considered when interpreting in situ, remote-sensing, and model estimates of dust optical properties.

explanation: 该研究涉及在德国Schauinsland站进行的大气CO2和CH4的长期测量，并与不同高度的进气口进行了比较，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和大气成分分析密切相关。
authors: Julian Großmann;Frank Meinhardt;Antje Hoheisel;Bryan Hellack;Martina Schmidt
title: Atmospheric CO2 and CH4 measurements at Schauinsland station, Germany: a comparative study of diurnal and seasonal variations at 12 and 35 m intake height
abstract:
Long-term measurements of atmospheric CO2 have been conducted at Schauinsland station in southwest Germany since 1972. In order possibly to relocate the air intake line from 12 m to 35 m above ground, we compared three years of parallel CO2 and CH4 measurements. We find systematic differences in diurnal and seasonal variations for CO2, but not for CH4. The results of our study indicate that measurements should be taken at both heights to ensure consistency with historical records. 
 At the atmospheric monitoring station Schauinsland (Black Forest, Germany), high-precision long-term measurements of atmospheric CO2 and CH4 have been conducted since 1972 and 1991, respectively. An additional air intake at 35 m a.g.l. (above ground level) has been installed alongside the existing intake at 12 m a.g.l. in September 2021. To ensure consistency and continuity of the historic CO2 and CH4 time series, a three-year comparison between the two intake heights has been carried out. This revealed systematic differences in CO2 mole fractions between the two levels: During summer, daytime diurnal mean CO2 mole fractions at 35 m are up to 0.5 ppm higher, while night-time values are up to 1.1 ppm lower, compared to 12 m, resulting in smaller diurnal amplitudes at 35 m. Seasonal mean CO2 mole fractions are lowered by up to 0.36 ppm at 35 m relative to 12 m in summer, whereas no significant differences are observed in winter. The diurnal and seasonal mean CH4 mole fraction differences between the two intake heights are negligible. However, highly frequent CH4 spikes originating from nearby grazing cows, which are present only during the summer months, increase hourly mean mole fractions at 12 m by up to 38 ppb, while no significant influence is measured at 35 m. The REBS (Robust Extraction of the Baseline Signal) algorithm is applied to the minutely CH4 summer data at 12 m and proved to be an effective approach for identification of data affected by very local influences.

explanation: 该研究使用地面基于的天空辐射计观测zenith天空辐射的频谱特征，以区分晴朗和多云的天空条件。这直接与大气环境遥感技术相关，特别是空气质量监测和云检索。研究涉及的天空辐射测量和云检测方法对大气成分分析和气溶胶检索具有重要意义。

authors: Pradeep Khatri;Hitoshi Irie;Hiroshi Kobayashi;Isamu Morino;Yoshitaka Jin;Tadahiro Hayasaka;Hironobu Iwabuchi;Tamio Takamura;Yoshiki Takayama
title: Spectral signatures of zenith sky radiance from surface-based sky radiometers: implications for clear- and cloudy-sky detection
abstract:
This study investigates the spectral characteristics of zenith sky radiances under clear- and cloudy-sky conditions using SKYNET sky radiometer observations. It proposes a simple, physically interpretable method for distinguishing sky states and demonstrates that wavelength-dependent radiance information can support reliable sky-state detection across diverse atmospheric environments. 
 Accurate identification of clear- and cloudy-sky conditions is essential for reliable aerosol and cloud retrievals from ground-based remote sensing observations. This study investigates the spectral characteristics of zenith sky radiance measured by SKYNET sky radiometers and evaluates their potential for distinguishing clear- and cloudy-sky conditions. For a given wavelength pair, the spectral slope derived from the measured signals (mobs) was separated into atmospheric (matm) and wavelength-dependent instrumental (minst) contributions. Radiative transfer simulations demonstrated that matm is strongly negative under cloud-free conditions and systematically shifts toward less negative values under cloudy conditions, providing a physical basis for matm-based sky-state discrimination. Based on these theoretical analyses, together with observational analyses of spectral zenith radiances and the dependence of matm on solar geometry, aerosol properties, and cloud properties for obervation data at multiple sites representing diverse atmospheric environments, including urban, maritime, tropical continental, and polar regions, practical criteria using matm were developed to classify observations into clear, cloudy, and undetermined categories. All four wavelength pairs examined (0.400–0.675, 0.400–0.870, 0.500–0.675, and 0.500–0.870 µm) provided robust discrimination, with the 0.500–0.675 µm pair showing the best and most consistent overall performance across the observation sites. Independent validation using collocated direct normal irradiance measurements confirmed the physical consistency of the matm-based classification. Further comparison with an existing cloud-screening procedure showed good agreement in clear-sky aerosol data extracted using the newly developed method across diverse atmospheric environments. Overall, these results demonstrate that spectral zenith sky radiance can provide a simple and physically interpretable basis for clear- and cloudy-sky detection, provided that the wavelength-dependent instrumental contribution is appropriately characterized. Incorporating such spectral diagnostics into ground-based radiometric networks can improve cloud screening and enhance the reliability of long-term aerosol and cloud climatological analyses.

explanation: 该论文主要研究海堤对沿海湿地水文-生物地球化学条件的影响，虽然涉及水质和生态变化，但与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）关系不大。
authors: Bingnan Zhao;Zhijun Dai;Xixing Liang;Wensheng Zhang;Fangbing Xu;Xuefei Mei;Sergio Fagherazzi
title: Seawall‐Induced Isolation Alters Hydrological‐Biogeochemical Conditions in Coastal Wetlands
abstract: Coastal wetlands are increasingly impacted by tropical cyclones and storm surges. Seawalls and levees built to reduce these hazards disconnect wetlands from adjacent uplands, yet their hydroecological effects remain poorly understood. Using continuous hydrological observations in Chongming Island, Changjiang Estuary, China, we compared seaward and landward wetlands separated by a seawall. CTD sensor data, water quality measurements, and plot surveys revealed that seawall construction weakens tidal connectivity and reduces hydrological exchange landward. Seaward wetlands exhibit tidal‐dominated dynamics with higher salinity and lower chlorophyll (CHL), chemical oxygen demand (COD), and total organic carbon (TOC), associated with presence of Phragmites australis. Interior wetlands show reduced salinity, higher values of CHL, COD and TOC, stronger rainfall‐driven responses, and are characterized by more terrestrial vegetation species. These findings suggest that seawalls can substantially alter wetland hydrodynamics and ecosystem structure, highlighting the importance of incorporating hydrological connectivity into seawall design to sustain wetland functions.

authors: Yingli Zhu;Weiqing Han;Jianing Wang;Jian Zheng;D. L. Suhas;Aneesh C. Subramanian;Lai‐yung Ruby Leung;Oluwayemi Garuba;Karthik Balaguru
title: Decadal Sea Level Variability Along the U.S. East Coast: Roles of Extratropical Versus Tropical Climate Modes Over the North Atlantic Ocean
abstract: Coastal decadal sea level anomalies (SLAs) in the U.S. east coast (USEC) play a critical role in modulating coastal flooding frequency, yet relative influences of tropical versus extratropical climate modes over the North Atlantic remain unresolved. By integrating observations, simulations from simplified dynamical models and climate models, we show that remote forcings drive the most USEC decadal SLAs since 1950, with approximately half of this signal transmitted via westward‐propagating Rossby waves. Notably, the tropical climate modes, the Atlantic Meridional Mode (AMM) and Atlantic Nino, exert comparable remote influences as the extratropical climate modes in the USEC. We identify a key mechanism that AMM‐related wind and buoyancy forcings act constructively in the northwest Atlantic, amplifying decadal SLAs in the north USEC. Our findings reveal that tropical Atlantic variability is an important, yet previously underappreciated, driver of regional sea level, underscoring its critical role in decadal predictions and flood risk assessments.

authors: Hugo Bellenger;Virginie Capelle;Jean‐Michel Hartmann
title: Enhancement of the Nighttime Ocean Cool Skin Effect by Natural Surfactants
abstract: The ocean interface brightness temperature is sensitive to the biologic activity reflected by the chlorophyll‐a concentration (Chla) in the upper layers of the oceans. This is shown using sea surface skin temperatures Tskin retrieved from spectra recorded by the Infrared Atmospheric Sounder Interferometer and collocated measurements of bulk temperatures Tbulk by drifters and of Chla from a daily Copernicus multi‐satellite product. The results demonstrate that |ΔTobs| $\vert {\Delta }{T}_{\text{obs}}\vert $, with ΔTobs=Tskin−Tbulk<0 ${\Delta }{T}_{\text{obs}}={T}_{\text{skin}}-{T}_{\text{bulk}}\,<  0$, increases with Chla, particularly when the surface wind is weak. This finding is attributed to the hydrodynamic damping of ocean near surface turbulence by biogenic surfactants that leads to an increase of the cool‐skin thickness. Parametric formulations of the cool skin temperature difference and thickness depending on both the wind speed and Chla are proposed. This enables to assess the global potential impact of biogenic surfactants on interfacial temperatures that is mostly a coastal and polar phenomenon.

authors: Mengze Li;Lin Liu;Chengyan Fan;Reynald Delaloye;Zhangyu Sun;Line Rouyet
title: Correcting Unwrapping Errors Toward Reliable Rock Glacier Velocity From InSAR Time Series
abstract: Rock Glacier Velocity is an Essential Climate Variable Permafrost Quantity, providing a quantifiable indicator of mountain permafrost evolution. Despite its wide usage, multi‐temporal InSAR often substantially underestimates rock glacier velocities compared to ground‐based measurements, limiting its reliability. In this study, we identified ubiquitous unwrapping errors in Sentinel‐1 interferograms as the dominant source of underestimation over 17 rock glaciers in the European Alps. To address this issue, we developed a method combining manual correction for short‐span interferograms and phase‐closure‐based correction for long‐span interferograms. Our method substantially mitigated velocity underestimation for the rock glacier Grosses Gufer, increasing the maximum velocity from ∼0.5 to ∼2.5 m/yr and achieving strong agreement with independent GNSS data (R2=0.79 ${R}^{2}=0.79$, p<0.01 $p<  0.01$) for velocities ≤2.5m/yr ${\le} 2.5\,\text{m/yr}$. This approach provides an important step toward reliable construction of Rock Glacier Velocity time series using InSAR, enhancing its application in alpine permafrost studies.

title: The 2 May 2025 Mw 7.4 Drake Passage Earthquake: Insights Into Tectonics at the Shackleton Fracture Zone–Chilean Trench Transition
abstract: On 2 May 2025, an Mw 7.4 earthquake occurred ∼120 km off the southern tip of Tierra del Fuego, at the transition of the Shackleton Fracture Zone and the Chile Trench. This event exhibits reverse‐faulting mechanisms with relatively steeply dipping planes and is the largest recorded along this complex plate boundary. Most aftershocks have similar mechanisms, although some show strike‐slip and normal faulting. To better resolve the activated fault system under limited station coverage, we relocated events and incorporated pP‐sP phases identified using a trained classifier to refine focal depths. A multichannel seismic reflection line provides additional insights into the structure of the subduction complex. We infer that the mainshock nucleated on the subduction interface or within the plate of the southernmost Chilean subduction system, with aftershocks marking activation of steeper structures. This behavior emphasizes how convergent and strike‐slip fault systems interact to complicate earthquake rupture at plate boundary transitions.

authors: Pengliang Yu;Matthew Roseboom;Ankur Mali;Jacques Rivière;Parisa Shokouhi;Chris Marone;Derek Elsworth
title: Magnitudes and Rates of Strength‐Drawdown Modulate Injection‐Induced Seismicity
abstract: Accurately forecasting injection‐induced seismicity remains a major challenge that is critically important for energy production and storage as controlling mechanisms are complex and remain opaque. We clarify key processes by following time‐histories of bespoke parameters anticipated to control strength reduction (drawdown) through overpressure during fluid injection. Injection‐driven radial overpressure fields motivate key parameter groups representing magnitudes (r∂P∂r $r\frac{\partial P}{\partial r}$) and rates (t∂P∂t $t\frac{\partial P}{\partial t}$) of strength‐drawdown. We emphasize these physics‐informed features as inputs embedded in a two‐stage machine learning (ML) architecture applied to high‐resolution microseismic and injection data from the Utah FORGE and EGS Collab stimulation experiments. Permuted models, selectively including then excluding these physically‐inspired terms, predict temporal seismic evolution and capture trends and peaks with testable and discernible fidelity. Improved predictions result from including these diagnostic parameters—confirming that the derived physical parameters mechanistically mediate seismicity. The magnitude of strength drawdown (r∂P∂r $r\frac{\partial P}{\partial r}$) dictates the size and localization of seismic events during phases of steep spatial pressurization—particularly early in the injection phase near the well. Conversely, t∂P∂t $t\frac{\partial P}{\partial t}$ governs the timing and rate of onset of seismic activity during rapid injection transients, accounting for elapsed‐time effects. Our approach demonstrates the broader benefits of embedding physics‐guided features into ML frameworks toward mitigation of seismic hazard.

authors: Shaofeng Hua;Baojun Chen;Jing Yang;Shujing Shen;Weiguo Liu;Yueqin Shi;Yubao Liu;Ping Tian;Xijing Liu;Yunfei Che
title: A Hybrid Superdroplet–Bin Microphysics Approach Reveals How Large Salt Particles Trigger Rain in Non‐Precipitating Warm Convective Clouds
abstract: This study develops a Superdroplet‐Bin hybrid microphysics scheme within the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model to investigate hygroscopic seeding of warm convective clouds. The Super‐droplet method describes 3D transport, deliquescence, condensation, and collision‐coalescence growth of seeding agents or solution droplets, while the spectral bin method simulates liquid‐phase processes. Idealized simulations indicate that seeding full‐spectrum salt near cloud base can produce a maximum accumulated precipitation of 11.59 mm in 3 h. Further sensitivity experiments on seeding particle size reveal that rainfall enhancement primarily originates from particles ≥4 μm, with 5 μm yielding the most pronounced effect. This is because particles ≥4 μm can nucleate to form droplets ≥20 μm, shifting collision‐coalescence from the low‐efficiency regime below 20 μm to the high‐efficiency regime between large and drizzle‐sized droplets. The tail and rain‐embryo effects are identified as the dominant mechanisms, competition alone cannot effectively broaden the droplet spectrum or trigger precipitation.

authors: Qidi Pan;Junran Li;Qiangqiang Sun;Danfeng Sun;Jinbao Li;Heqiang Du;Huijie Xiao;Huixin Zhu;Lexin Li
title: An Improved Dust Emission Modeling With Multiple Endmember Spectral Mixture Analysis
abstract: Traditional dust emission schemes typically rely on photosynthetic vegetation (PV) alone when parameterizing key surface properties. Here, we integrate five endmembers from the multiple endmember spectral mixture analysis (MESMA), namely PV, non‐photosynthetic vegetation, bare soil, dark surface, and ice/snow (IS), into a well‐established dust emission scheme to simultaneously constrain surface roughness and the erodible fraction, avoiding the common reliance on PV alone as in traditional dust emission schemes. By evaluating three severe dust events in East Asia in 2021, 2023, and 2024, the MESMA‐constrained configurations reduce total dust emissions by 22.2%–49.7% and show substantially improved agreement with station observations. By enabling a physically realistic characterization of dryland surface heterogeneity through multiple endmembers, this approach substantially alleviates the systematic overestimation that is typical when using PV‐based parameterizations.

authors: Jing‐Yi Zhuo;Chia‐Ying Lee;Suzana J. Camargo;Adam H. Sobel;Gabriel A. Vecchi
title: Impacts of Sea Surface Temperature Warming Pattern Biases on Tropical Cyclone Activity and Hazard
abstract: Most climate models simulate greater warming in the equatorial eastern Pacific than in the west under historical forcing, resulting in a reduced zonal sea surface temperature (SST) gradient and a weakened Walker circulation. This contrasts with observed trends and highlights a persistent model–observation discrepancy with far‐reaching impacts on regional climate extremes. The authors' previous work showed that reducing mean‐state biases in a coupled model yields SST trends more consistent with observations. Here, we downscale tropical cyclones (TCs) from these simulations and find that a strengthened zonal SST gradient is associated with increased TC frequency and hazards in the North Atlantic and suppresses activity in the South Pacific. In future projections, both biased and bias‐corrected models simulate relative eastern Pacific warming, yet their TC responses differ regionally, with the bias‐corrected model projecting greater TC activity and hazards over the North Atlantic.

authors: Haibing Yu;Xin Luo
title: A Generalized Analytical Model for Marine Gas Hydrate Stability Zones With Thermodynamically Constrained Pressure–Temperature Phase Boundary
abstract: Accurate thermodynamic delineation of marine gas hydrate stability zones (GHSZs) is a fundamental prerequisite for assessing methane hydrate inventories, quantifying the vulnerability of methane dissociation to climate change, and evaluating overpressure‐induced submarine geohazards. However, the commonly adopted pressure–temperature phase boundaries are predominantly calibrated under idealized conditions and fail to capture natural marine conditions, leading to persistent uncertainties and systematic biases in global GHSZ delineation. Here, we assemble a globally representative dataset of field‐constrained hydrate records to refine and calibrate a thermodynamically constrained phase boundary tailored to natural marine environments. The resulting field‐calibrated phase boundary features clear physical interpretability, robust extrapolation reliability, and enables the GHSZ boundary depth to be calculated directly using an explicit closed‐from analytical solution. The analytical model delineates thermodynamically admissible GHSZ configurations and is validated against global observations for the prevalent single basal‐interface case, providing an efficient framework for regional‐to‐global hydrate‐related assessments.

authors: K. Németh;E. Williams;Q. Wang;A. Neska;G. Sátori;M. Herein;T. Haszpra;P. Steinbach;T. Bozóki
title: Daily Peak Activity of the African Lightning Chimney Based on Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Lightning Imager (LI), World Wide Lightning Location Network (WWLLN), and Schumann Resonance (SR) Observations
abstract: Lightning activity is strongly concentrated in tropical continental “chimneys”, among which the African lightning chimney stands out as the most intense globally. However, until recently, the incomplete and spatially uneven detection efficiency of ground‐based lightning networks, together with the limited spatio‐temporal coverage of satellite observations, have constrained the quantitative characterization of African lightning activity, particularly on the daily timescales. Since July 2024, the Lightning Imager (LI) onboard the Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) satellite has provided the first continuous, high‐temporal‐resolution observations of lightning activity over Africa and Europe from geostationary orbit. In this paper, we examine, based on the first year of MTG LI observations, how consistently daily peak activity in the African lightning chimney is represented in different observational data sets. For this purpose, we use MTG LI group and flash data, together with World Wide Lightning Location Network (WWLLN) stroke observations and Schumann resonance (SR) measurements, and focus on two key parameters: the daily peak activity and its timing. We find that daily peak activity derived from MTG flashes shows a strong positive correlation with SR intensity (r = 0.749), while WWLLN stroke observations show much weaker correspondence. The timing of the daily peak is broadly consistent across the data sets, with the best agreement observed between MTG flashes and SR intensity. For all data sets, daily peak activity is strongly correlated with total daily activity. The strong correspondence between MTG flashes and SR intensity supports the use of both data sets in characterizing the daily activity of the African lightning chimney.

title: Overestimation of Cloud Sensitivity in Orographic Clouds Over the Southern Tibetan Plateau Due To Neglected Dynamical Constraints
abstract: Accurately quantifying cloud sensitivity (Saci), the relative change in cloud droplet number with aerosol loading, is essential for reducing uncertainties in aerosol–cloud interactions. However, its dependence on cloud dynamics is often overlooked, causing biases in estimates of Saci and Twomey effect radiative forcing (RFaci). Using in situ observations of orographic clouds over the southern Tibetan Plateau (STP), we estimate cloud‐base updraft velocity (w) from the water vapor supersaturation budget and examine how Saci varies with w. Results reveal that Saci follows a sigmoid pattern with increasing w. Driven by Köhler activation theory and its mathematical definition, this pattern is theoretically expected to potentially hold across diverse cloud regimes. Ignoring this dependence yields a 14%–40% overestimate of Saci for STP shallow orographic clouds, which may consequently bias local estimates of RFaci. These findings provide new insights into quantifying cloud sensitivity, while their global applicability and implications require further observational validation.

title: Global Assessment and Error Budget of EarthCARE Column Aerosol Optical Depth: Physical Limits and Quantitative Mitigation
abstract: The Earth Cloud Aerosol and Radiation Explorer (EarthCARE) provides critical spaceborne high spectral resolution LiDAR observations for global aerosol profiling. However, integrating these vertically resolved aerosol extinction coefficient profiles into column Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) introduces systematic biases from physical observation boundaries, which currently lack global validation and quantitative attribution. This study presents a global assessment and error budget of EarthCARE 355 nm column AOD using solar and lunar AErosol Robotic NETwork measurements from August 2024 to March 2026. Baseline validations demonstrate robust spatiotemporal tracking capabilities (daytime R = 0.873, nighttime R = 0.859) and physically consistent independently retrieved LiDAR ratio distributions across coarse and fine mode aerosol regimes. Nevertheless, cross‐framework comparisons show that complex absorbing mixtures are frequently assigned to fine mode dominant EarthCARE categories. Concurrently, a pervasive systematic underestimation persists globally (daytime MB = −0.060, nighttime MB = −0.073). Mechanistically, this underestimation is associated with three distinct physical limits: near‐surface clutter truncation (0–400 m), free‐tropospheric signal‐to‐noise ratio detection limits, and attenuation‐induced sampling biases under extreme aerosol loading (AOD > 1.0). Applying a constant boundary‐layer geometric extrapolation mitigates the near‐surface truncation, reducing the daytime MB by ∼40% (to −0.036) and recovering the linear regression slope from 0.67 to 0.77 while preserving high R. Further, compensating for free‐tropospheric background detection limit reduces the ubiquitous underestimation by an additional ∼17% (+0.010). This physically based error‐budget framework quantifies the major recoverable contributions and characterizes the factors associated with the remaining bias, providing a robust basis for optimizing future spaceborne LiDAR retrievals.

title: Extreme Atmospheric Moistening and Drying Events at Ny‐Ålesund and Their Relation to Weather Systems
abstract: Understanding the role of water vapor in Arctic amplification requires a detailed evaluation of its spatio‐temporal variability. In this work, we use an integrated water vapor (IWV) data set from a ground‐based microwave radiometer at Ny‐Ålesund, Svalbard, covering 2012–2024, to characterize temporal IWV variability. We also identify extreme atmospheric moistening and drying events based on a new detection method and relate them to large‐scale circulation patterns and airmass pathways. IWV exhibits a pronounced annual cycle with values ranging from 0.6 to 33 kg m−2 ${\mathrm{m}}^{-2}$. While absolute IWV variability within a month is smaller in winter than in summer, relative variability is nearly twice as large. We identified 352 extreme moistening and 371 extreme drying events, accounting for 20% of the study period. Extreme drying occurs primarily through continuous drying, whereas extreme moistening events include a higher fraction of consecutive moistening episodes and therefore last longer. Most events occur on synoptic time scales of 1–3 days. Extreme moistening events are linked to large‐scale circulation patterns that facilitate the advection of moist airmasses toward Svalbard from southeasterly to westerly directions, which account for 52% of all moistening events. Extreme drying occurs under similar circulation patterns, but is mainly linked to a reduction in the poleward moisture transport due to an eastward shift of the prevailing pressure centers. 45% of extreme drying events follow directly after an extreme moistening event. Given the comprehensive ground‐based observations available at Ny‐Ålesund, the identified events provide a useful framework to study their impact on clouds, precipitation, radiation, and surface conditions.

title: PROSAIL5B‐DR: A Radiative Transfer Model Extension for Dust Retention Effects on Vegetation Spectra
abstract: Dust deposition on urban vegetation alters canopy spectral reflectance and can reduce the reliability of parameter retrieval based on radiative transfer models (RTMs). However, conventional RTMs, including the coupled PROSPECT–SAIL (PROSAIL) model, do not explicitly represent these external optical effects. We developed PROSAIL5B‐DR by incorporating a dust‐induced absorption term into the leaf absorption coefficient, allowing dust effects to propagate to canopy reflectance. The dust mass‐specific absorption coefficient was calculated using the Mie theory. We evaluated model performance across dust retention levels, vegetation types, and urban environments. PROSAIL5B‐DR reproduced canopy spectral responses more accurately than PROSAIL5B while preserving the original model structure. It also reduced the simulation bias that increased with dust retention without adding redundant parameters. Explicitly representing retained particulate matter therefore improves canopy spectral simulations and provides a physically based approach for assessing vegetation optical properties in polluted urban environments.

title: Climatology of Atmospheric Boundary Layer Height Over Nearshore and Open Ocean Regions of the Western North Pacific
abstract: Atmospheric boundary layer height (ABLH) plays an important role in air–sea interactions and regional climate over the western North Pacific (WNP). Using ERA5 reanalysis data from 1979 to 2025, this paper investigates the interannual variability, monthly variations, and seasonal spatial patterns of ABLH. To explore potential drivers of ABLH variability, correlation analyses are conducted between ABLH and three key predictors: wind shear, surface sensible heat flux (HFX) and Brunt–Väisälä frequency (N2). In addition, records from nearshore (NS) and open ocean (OS) stations are analyzed to examine spatial differences in ABLH behavior. The results reveal clear regional differences. Open ocean ABLH increases consistently during both daytime and nighttime, with mean changes of 17.07 and 14.91 m per decade, respectively. Nearshore changes are weaker, particularly at night. Open ocean ABLH is generally highest in winter and lowest in summer, whereas NS ABLH exhibits a mixed land–sea seasonal pattern, with relatively high values commonly occurring around September and October. The controlling factors also vary by region and season. Open ocean ABLH is strongly associated with wind shear and N2, with mechanical forcing becoming particularly important in winter. In contrast, NS daytime ABLH is primarily associated with HFX, while the influence of wind shear becomes more pronounced at night. The findings contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the marine ABL and provide valuable insights for its modeling, OS wind energy assessment, and pollutant dispersion studies.

title: Aerosol Retrieval Over Ocean From DPC‐2/GF‐5(02): Using RemoTAP Extended With a 3‐Parameter Ocean Bio‐Optical Model and Comparisons With a 1‐Parameter Model
abstract: Multi‐angle polarimetric instruments (MAPs) enable the retrieval of essential aerosol properties over oceanic regions. MAPs retrieval algorithms commonly use a 1‐parameter ocean bio‐optical model (OBM), based on chlorophyll‐a concentration only to represent optical properties over open waters (case‐1), whereas the coastal water (mixture of case‐1 and case‐2 waters) representation generally requires multi‐parameter models as demonstrated for sophisticated sensors such as SPEXone. In this study, we investigated whether meaningful improvements in aerosol retrieval over coastal waters can be achieved using data from the Directional Polarization Camera DPC‐2, with a relatively limited spectral configuration, by the addition of bio‐optical degrees of freedom. To this end, the Remote Sensing of Trace Gases and Aerosol Products (RemoTAP) algorithm, developed by the Space Research Organization Netherlands (SRON), is extended by incorporating a 3‐parameter OBM to represent coastal waters. The three parameters are chlorophyll‐a concentration, backscattering coefficient of particulate matter at 660 nm, and the absorption coefficient of non‐algal particles (NAP) and colored dissolved organic matter (CDOM) at 440 nm. We applied the extended algorithm for aerosol retrieval from synthetic and real DPC‐2 observations. Results were compared with those using the 1‐parameter OBM and retrieval results from real observations were evaluated using colocated coastal AERONET data over case‐1 and case‐2 waters. The most important finding from this work is that a simple open ocean 1‐parameter OBM together with fitting a wavelength‐dependent Lambertian correction term provides sufficient accuracy for global aerosol retrieval using DPC‐2 data, even over coastal water.

title: Evidence for multi-Li<sup>+</sup> clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes
abstract:
Machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations, spectroscopy, electrochemical data and quantum-chemical calculations reveal previously unstudied multi-lithium-ion complexes without bound anions, improving understanding of lithium-ion-battery functionality at the atomic level. 
 In lithium-ion batteries, the bulk solvation structure of the electrolyte is a major determinant of the physical and electrochemical properties of the cell, for example, conductivity, viscosity, salt dissociation and subsequent reactivity, the electrochemical stability window (and thus solid electrolyte interphase formation), and the composition of the electrochemical double layer1–3. However, elucidation of this structure at an atomic level of detail has been challenging to accomplish via a purely experimental approach. Here we combine machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations4–16, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, electrochemical data3,17–20 and quantum-chemical calculations to reveal previously unstudied multi-Li+ complexes without bound anions that are uniquely facile for reduction. This insight explains the success of empirically chosen ethylene-carbonate-containing solvent mixtures and provides a foundation for the rational design of improved electrolytes. Furthermore, our machine-learning force-field-based lithium-ion-battery electrolyte simulations accurately reproduce a wide range of condensed-phase experiments3,21–24, despite being parameterized to only quantum-chemical gas-phase cluster calculations, and hence provide a compelling demonstration that machine-learning force-field-based models developed from first principles can robustly represent a complex chemical system to atomic resolution. Machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations, spectroscopy, electrochemical data and quantum-chemical calculations reveal previously unstudied multi-lithium-ion complexes without bound anions, improving understanding of lithium-ion-battery functionality at the atomic level.

title: Evaluating space-based methane detection through a one-year blind test
abstract:
A year-long single-blind study shows that multiple satellites can accurately detect and quantify methane point-source emissions. 
 Space-based remote sensing allows detection and monitoring of large, concentrated methane sources worldwide1. However, independent evaluation of instruments and algorithms is limited, and new satellites and artificial intelligence techniques have not been tested under controlled, single-blind conditions2. Here we conduct a year-long, single-blind test involving 746 events: 481 methane releases of 9.5–1,183.7 kg h−1 and 265 blank controls. We released metered methane quantities in Arizona, USA, coinciding with overpasses from 12 government, commercial and non-profit satellites. Fifteen analysis teams from nine countries generated more than 2,250 estimates, making this, to our knowledge, the largest controlled test so far and one of the first evaluations of the instruments EMIT, Tanager-1 (Carbon Mapper) and GHOSt. Performance is heterogeneous: ‘built-for-purpose’ instruments designed to target methane demonstrate excellent detection performance (92–100% true positive rate, 0–11% false positive rate) and quantification accuracy (slope 0.83–1.00, 44% mean absolute percentage error). Instruments repurposed for methane sensing perform more variably (detection rates 62–88%, 46% mean absolute percentage error); still, many demonstrate significant skill. Broad land scanners detect poorly at tested rates but have consistent global coverage and historical archives, motivating additional work. Artificial intelligence-based methods show promise, but caution is warranted; 79% of false positives emerge from these methods. Ground-measured cloud cover >20% degraded performance across systems, raising concerns for use in some locations. Our findings show that satellite-based measurements can achieve accurate detection and quantification of methane point sources when the source location is approximately known. A year-long single-blind study shows that multiple satellites can accurately detect and quantify methane point-source emissions.

title: Intrinsic physicochemical activity at microplastic–water interfaces
abstract:
Commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity at water interfaces, manifested by spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species, challenging the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, with implications for human health and the environment. 
 Plastics have become an integral part of our modern society, largely because they are generally regarded as chemically inert under normal circumstances. However, plastics fragmented into microplastics (less than 5 mm in size) have recently raised significant public concerns, and have been detected widely across ecosystems and human tissues with increasing environmental and health risks1–5. Here we show that commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity in water, manifested by the spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species that increases with interfacial hydrophobicity and strongly correlates with interfacial electrostatics. Ab initio calculations support these observations and reveal that hydroxide oxidation becomes energetically more favourable at increasingly hydrophobic microplastic–water interfaces through the combined effects of partial solvation and electrostatics. These interfacial properties and the resulting oxidative chemistry have direct implications for biomolecular adsorption, protein aggregation, and even cellular damage. Together, our findings challenge the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, identify a possibly overlooked mechanism for the detrimental effects of microplastics on health and the environment, and contribute to a fundamental understanding of the structure–activity relationship of interfacial water, which may inform the design of safer and more sustainable plastic materials. Commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity at water interfaces, manifested by spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species, challenging the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, with implications for human health and the environment.

title: Hidden reaction pathways inform additive engineering for perovskite LEDs
abstract:
Resolution and control of the hidden solution-phase chemistry of 5-aminovaleric acid added to perovskite precursor solutions is described for producing films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield and near-infrared perovskite LEDs with enhanced external quantum efficiencies. 
 Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) have emerged as a promising class of solution-processed light-emitting devices, combining high efficiency with facile fabrication1–5. Amino-acid-based molecular additives are widely used to regulate crystallization and suppress defects in perovskite thin films6–8, yet these molecules are chemically reactive in precursor solutions, in which their transformations and products remain poorly understood. Here we resolve and control the hidden solution-phase chemistry of a ubiquitous additive, 5-aminovaleric acid (5AVA), whose solution-phase reactivity has remained unclear6,9–15. We show that 5AVA undergoes competing in situ reactions during precursor preconditioning, yielding two chemically and functionally distinct products: a beneficial organoamidinium zwitterion and a detrimental Lewis-base lactam. By explaining this reaction dichotomy and establishing targeted reaction-pathway control, we selectively use the beneficial species. Direct synthesis and incorporation of the purified zwitterion decouple its intrinsic passivation function from confounding by-products, yielding perovskite films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 97.2% and PeLEDs with a champion external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 37.1%, alongside a mean peak EQE of 32.8%. Finally, we demonstrate that this reaction-pathway control concept can be extended to further additive chemistries and emission colours, highlighting its potential as a chemistry-driven strategy for rational additive design in PeLEDs. Resolution and control of the hidden solution-phase chemistry of 5-aminovaleric acid added to perovskite precursor solutions is described for producing films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield and near-infrared perovskite LEDs with enhanced external quantum efficiencies.

title: Clasping folds enable superior elastic strength of graphene films
abstract:
Two-dimensional graphene films with unusual folded surfaces are synthesized through a modular assembly strategy and show enhanced strength, toughness and elastic strain owing to stress distribution between interlayer folds. 
 Two-dimensional graphene sheets show strong potential for use in fabrication of macroscopic films, as they have exceptional mechanical properties owing to their in-plane strength1–6. Improvements in the stacking order of flat two-dimensional sheets have led to corresponding improvements in the strength and toughness of such films7–11. In addition, modulation of the spatial conformation of individual units has enabled the development of benchmark materials with superior properties12,13; however, this has remained elusive in the case of two-dimensional sheets. Here we report a strategy for preparation of graphene films with a combination of high strength (2.9 GPa), toughness (84.5 MJ m−3) and elastic strain (5%). We attribute these performance gains to a fold-clasping lamellar structure achieved by modular assembly of surface-folded multilayer graphene oxide flakes. We identify a pull-to-push transition of force chain topology and propose a shear-lock stress transfer strategy in the fold-clasping lamellar graphene film that enables advances in mechanical properties. This work demonstrates the modular design of spatial conformation of two-dimensional flakes on a large scale and further improves the performance of macroscopic films for potential applications in lightweight structural components. Two-dimensional graphene films with unusual folded surfaces are synthesized through a modular assembly strategy and show enhanced strength, toughness and elastic strain owing to stress distribution between interlayer folds.

title: Progressive oxidative weathering raised sub-arc mantle fugacity on the Archaean Earth
abstract:
Progressive oxidative weathering in the Archaean may have raised the proportion of oxidized sulfur recycled during subduction, suggesting a feedback between the surface and increasingly oxidized arc magmatism, according to sulfur in apatite inclusions. 
 In the modern Earth, sub-arc mantle oxygen fugacity is intrinsically associated with addition of sulfur species by slab fluids. However, it is unclear to what extent recycling of volatiles controlled redox changes of the sub-arc mantle in the early Earth. Here we use sulfur K-edge micro-X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy to measure the relative abundances of S6+, S4+ and S2− in apatite inclusions hosted by geochemically characterized and dated zircons from sub-arc sanukitoid magmas that span 3.4 billion years of Earth’s geological history. The sub-arc mantle shows marked increase in oxygen fugacity between 3.4 and 3.0 billion years ago (Ga). It is substantially more oxidized than unaltered ambient upper mantle, a characteristic that cannot be explained by fractionation, degassing or intrinsic mantle processes. We propose that progressive oxidative weathering enhanced the proportion of oxidized sulfur recycled to mantle wedge sources, establishing feedback between subduction of surface materials and incrementally oxidized arc magmatism. Early subduction involving inorganic oxidation and ‘whiffs’ of oxygen between 3.4 and 2.7 Ga may have regulated an early increase in fugacity of the sub-arc mantle before the Great Oxidation Event, matching similar conditions to the modern Earth by 2.1 Ga. Progressive oxidative weathering in the Archaean may have raised the proportion of oxidized sulfur recycled during subduction, suggesting a feedback between the surface and increasingly oxidized arc magmatism, according to sulfur in apatite inclusions.

title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
abstract:
Edematous malnutrition in children has unclear causes. Here, the authors show that genetic variation at one‑carbon metabolism genes influences disease risk through homocysteine‑related pathways and ancestry‑linked effects in affected populations. 
 Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1, PRICKLE2, GABBR2, and PLD2, with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk. Edematous malnutrition in children has unclear causes. Here, the authors show that genetic variation at one‑carbon metabolism genes influences disease risk through homocysteine‑related pathways and ancestry‑linked effects in affected populations.

title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
abstract:
This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity. 
 Chiral amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceutical synthesis. (R)-3-([1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)-2-aminopropan-1-ol (ABP), a key chiral amine intermediate of the drug Entresto, has remained difficult to access via enzymatic asymmetric synthesis due to the inability of ω-transaminases to accommodate its bulky ketone precursor. Here, we engineer an ω-transaminase from Bacillus megaterium by integrating Funnel metadynamics, PathDetect-SOM, and path collective variables to reconstruct the free energy surface of substrate binding, pinpointing high-energy barrier regions of the binding process and the trade-off between tunnel accessibility and productive binding. Dynamic cross-correlation network analysis further identifies distal regulatory sites governing these bottleneck regions. Iterative experimental optimization yields the 13M variant, exhibiting catalytic activity 106 times that of the wild type with >99% enantiomeric excess, enabling the efficient enzymatic asymmetric synthesis of ABP. This integrated computational-experimental framework for resolving the tunnel-pocket binding trade-off offers a generalizable strategy for engineering ω-transaminases toward bulky substrates in green pharmaceutical synthesis. This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity.

title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
abstract:
A new spectroscopic method for tomographic mapping of the 3D orientation of nanocrystals reveals complex structures and dynamics in both spontaneously formed and externally driven assemblies in soft matter. 
 Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes. A new spectroscopic method for tomographic mapping of the 3D orientation of nanocrystals reveals complex structures and dynamics in both spontaneously formed and externally driven assemblies in soft matter.

title: Citizens’ assemblies propose ambitious climate policy but impacts remain limited
abstract:
Deliberative citizen participation, such as climate assemblies, has been promoted in climate governance. This study finds that, although assemblies proposed more ambitious recommendations than existing climate policy, these recommendations rarely translated into actual policy decisions. 
 Climate citizens’ assemblies convene randomly selected citizens who, after structured learning and deliberation, develop policy recommendations. Yet, whether they produce more ambitious recommendations and influence political decisions remains contested. Here we conduct a comparative, counterfactual assessment of 488 recommendations from five national and one state-level assembly in Western Europe, drawing on document analysis and expert interviews. The results show that citizens consistently proposed more ambitious climate measures than existing government policy. Recommendations sometimes influenced policy by adding momentum, enriching plans, breaking deadlocks or introducing novel ideas, but such influence was rare. Only the French assembly shows substantial policy impact, with one-third of its recommendations having influenced policy, due to strong power delegation, political leadership and resulting public pressure. In the other cases, policy impact was minimal or absent. These findings show that citizens’ assemblies can raise policy ambition, but translating recommendations into political decisions depends strongly on political conditions. Deliberative citizen participation, such as climate assemblies, has been promoted in climate governance. This study finds that, although assemblies proposed more ambitious recommendations than existing climate policy, these recommendations rarely translated into actual policy decisions.

title: Assessing green-growth and degrowth pathways through institutional regime feasibility
abstract:
Choosing a feasible economic growth trajectory to mitigate climate change cannot hinge on only gross domestic product trends. This Perspective presents a framework to understand where each possible growth path places its heaviest burdens and shows that such understanding is critical to inform policy decisions. 
 Whether climate change policy should pursue green growth, degrowth, post-growth or agrowth cannot be settled by gross domestic product trajectories. The decisive issue is where each pathway places its heaviest burdens: on technology, well-being generation, energy demand, institutional capacity or political credibility. We extend the Kaya identity by decomposing energy intensity into the well-being generated per unit of output and the energy required per unit of well-being. The split locates stylized burden positions; a subsequent regime-feasibility test asks which institutions can generate and sustain the required movements, who bears costs and risks, and whether commitments remain credible over time. title: Local control of Cre-regulated genetic modeling in vivo using wireless implantable optoelectronics
abstract: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. To address this, we developed E-LightR-Cre recombinase, enabling precise, spatially restricted gene activation with no dark-state activity and robust blue light responsiveness. To achieve local activation of E-LightR-Cre in specific organ sites, we engineered wireless, fully implantable optoelectronic devices enabling focal illumination of murine lungs with no discernible organ damage. The size of the activated area is controlled by modulating light intensity and duration. Using implanted optoelectronic devices, we activated E-LightR-Cre in a selected area of mouse lungs and achieved local regulation of targeted genes. Light-regulated expression of the oncogenic KRas-G12D mutant in mouse lungs induced local formation of oncogenic lesions. These results show that our protein engineering and adaptable optoelectronic approaches enable facile application of optogenetic tools for locally controlled disease modeling in vivo.

title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

authors: Yuhang Song;Claudia Marcolli;Jie Chen;Ulrike Lohmann
title: Ice nucleation by kaolinite: Morphology shapes the size dependence of ice nucleation active sites on dust particles
abstract: Mineral dusts are the most important type of ice-nucleating particles and play a key role in cloud formation and climate. Their activity is commonly assumed to scale with particle surface area, yet whether this assumption holds across particle sizes remains unverified. Here, we quantify size-dependent ice nucleation activity using compositionally pure, size-segregated kaolinite (KGa-1b). Ice nucleation active site (INAS) densities were determined for size classes from submicron to 48 μm, revealing two distinct ice-nucleation regimes. At low temperatures (∼240 K), INAS density per surface area is independent of particle size. In contrast, at warm temperatures (∼260 K), particles of 6 to 12 μm exhibit the highest INAS densities, up to two orders of magnitude greater than smaller particles and nonsize-selected bulk samples. Linking these results to particle morphology indicates that well-aligned, multilayered platelet edges provide the continuous hydroxylated surfaces required for efficient ice nucleation. Our findings demonstrate that morphology can modulate particle size–dependent ice nucleation, highlighting limitations of simple surface area–based parameterizations.

title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning
abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a “dirty” mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting “dirty” irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical “gene of scrap compatibility,” this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus(SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen’s diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

title: Bisulfate-mediated selective methane oxidation under mild aqueous conditions
abstract: The selective oxidation of methane under mild conditions remains a formidable challenge because of the inert C─H bond and the ease of over-oxidation. Here we report a facile strategy that enables methane conversion at room temperature and ambient pressure using molecular O2and commercially available Cu powder in dilute aqueous H2SO4. The reaction is capable of proceeding with only trace CO2formation, producing methyl bisulfate and methanol as the primary partial oxidation products. In situ Raman spectroscopy indicates that an in situ O2-derived Cu2O surface is the reaction-relevant phase associated with C─H bond activation. The observed selectivity arises from bisulfate adsorption on this Cu2O surface, which suppresses methanol over-oxidation, together with the interception of surface-generated methyl intermediates to form oxidation-resistant methyl bisulfate. This Cu/O2-H2SO4system demonstrates that methane can be selectively oxidized under mild aqueous conditions and provides mechanistic insight into Cu/O2-mediated oxidation, suggesting a bisulfate-assisted approach to suppressing over-oxidation that may be applicable to other substrates.

title: Nanoconfinement-cooperated catalysis enables rapid tandem redox kinetics for wide-temperature lithium-sulfur batteries
abstract: The slow kinetics of sulfur cathodes caused by the high energy barriers of Li+desolvation stem primarily from the structure of the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP). Herein, a synergistic strategy combining electrochemical tandem catalysis with spatial nanoconfinement is proposed to regulate the Li(solvent)x+dynamics. As a proof-of-concept, the porous covalent organic framework (denoted as TPBD) decorated MXene is in situ constructed, acting as a tandem kinetic promoter. The theoretical simulations and in situ Raman reveal that the porous TPBD layer confines the bulky Li(solvent)x+species and sieves the spatial structure with accelerated Li+diffusion kinetics. Meanwhile, MXene serves as a negatively charged substrate that helps disrupt anion-solvent interactions and reconstruct the solvation structure at the IHP, thereby enhancing Li+kinetics and sulfur redox reversibility. Encouragingly, the assembled cells demonstrate a superior Li+transference number (0.77), long-term cycling lifespan up to 1000 cycles, as well as excellent areal capacity (>6 mAh cm−2) at 0°C and superior rate capability at 50°C under a high sulfur loading of 7.51 mg cm−2. The as-prepared pouch cell remains stable for over 100 cycles, validating this novel integration of catalysis and nanoconfinement for tandem kinetics in Li-S batteries.

title: Emergent coherent-incoherent phonon crossover enables ultralow lattice thermal conductivity in 3D double perovskite
abstract: The interplay between coherent (wave-like) and incoherent (particle-like) phonon transport is central to heat conduction, yet experimental evidence of their crossover in bulk three-dimensional (3D) crystals remains scarce. Here, we report intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κκl) in the lead-free double perovskite Cs2AgBiCl6, reaching 0.52 and 0.28 W m−1K−1in single crystal and polycrystals, respectively, at room temperature. Combining thermal transport, low-temperature heat capacity, Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron x-ray pair distribution function analysis, and anharmonic lattice-dynamics calculations, we uncover the microscopic origin of this anomalous heat transport. Chemical bonding heterogeneity, weakly bound rattling-like Cs vibrations, anisotropic Cl dynamics, and soft lattice modes generate low-energy localized optical phonons that strongly interact with acoustic modes. Enhanced three- and four-phonon scattering suppresses phonon lifetimes, while anharmonic renormalization flattens optical branches and reduces group velocities. Coherent contributions account for ∼50% ofκκlnear room temperature and exceeding incoherent contributions above ∼200 K, revealing an emergent coherent-incoherent phonon crossover in a fully crystalline 3D solid.

title: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

title: Learning to infer transitively on a mental line in premotor cortex
abstract: Transitive inference (TI) is a form of deductive reasoning that enables the derivation of unknown relationships among premises. It is hypothesized that this cognitive process relies on mapping stimuli onto a “mental line,” a linear workspace organized by arbitrarily assigned ranks. However, its neural basis remains unclear: Does this mental line have a neural correlate and how is it learned? This study investigates the role of dorsal premotor cortex (PMd) in encoding the hypothesized mental line as monkeys acquire item relationships for motor decisions. Findings reveal that PMd multiunit activity organizes along a theoretically predicted direction, supporting a geometrical model that explains behavior. Moreover, a learning process is observed, where the mental line rotates to align with motor planning.

title: A fast and frugal Gaussian boson sampling emulator
abstract: Classical algorithms have successfully reproduced expectation values of observables for certain quantum circuits using off-the-shelf computing resources; however, matching the performance of the most advanced quantum devices on sampling problems typically incurs extreme memory and computational costs, restricting such simulations to only a handful of supercomputers worldwide. In this work, we demonstrate a classical simulation outperforming Gaussian boson sampling experiments of 100 modes on established benchmark tests using a single central processing unit (CPU) or graphics processing unit (GPU). Being embarrassingly parallelizable, a small number of CPUs or GPUs allows us to match previous sampling rates that required more than 100 GPUs. We believe that algorithmic and implementation improvements have the potential to generalize our tools to photocounting and pseudo–photon number–resolving scenarios and larger system sizes. Last, most of the innovations in our tools remain valid for generic probability distributions over binary variables, rendering them potentially applicable to the simulation of qubit-based sampling problems and creating classical surrogates for classical-quantum algorithms.

title: A transcriptional cofactor GRIP1 drives PPARγ DNA binding and p300-dependent enhancer activity during homeostatic macrophage polarization
abstract: Homeostatic macrophages maintain tissue health and resolve inflammation. Upon sustained exposure to type II cytokine IL4, transcription factors STAT6, KLF4, EGR2 and a ligand-regulated nuclear receptor PPARγ orchestrate the M2IL4‘polarization’, marked by enhancer RNA (eRNA) production near multiple M2 genes. The mechanisms of enhancer activation by unliganded PPARγ are poorly understood. We interrogated cofactor requirements for PPARγ-driven gene expression in M2IL4, including those lacking PPARγ or a ligand-dependent nuclear receptor coregulator NCoA2/GRIP1 vs. macrophages treated with the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone. As expected, rosiglitazone activated conventional PPARγ targets; GRIP1 deletion blunted their induction and depleted GRIP1-interacting histone acetyltransferase p300 from PPARγ-bound sites. Surprisingly, GRIP1 colocalized with unliganded PPARγ in M0 and M2IL4, and GRIP1 ablation dramatically reduced genome-wide DNA binding of PPARγ itself while promoting broad deposition of CTCF insulator. Functionally, GRIP1 deletion mirrored PPARγ deficiency, establishing GRIP1 as a central regulator of unliganded PPARγ DNA binding, required for both eRNA and mRNA transcription of PPARγ targets in homeostatic macrophages.

title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked. Demographic perspectives on ancient disasters are useful in generating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes.
